chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): From a man who prayed two rak'ahs in a garment in which there was janabah, then he learned of it.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'He must restart the prayer.'
I asked him about a man who was praying and in his garment was janabah or blood, until he finished his prayer, then he learned of it.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'His prayer has passed and there is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: Major ritual impurity requiring full body wash (ghusl)

ai.seo_question: Does a prayer become invalid if ritual impurity is discovered in the clothing after the prayer is completed?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the ruling of *al-ghafilah* (the unaware) in Shia jurisprudence, establishing that validity depends on the timing of discovery relative to the prayer's completion. It underscores the principle that ritual impurity in clothing does not invalidate the prayer unless discovered before the final *taslim*, reflecting the juristic preference for ease (*rukhas*) when the error was unintentional. This distinction is pivotal in distinguishing between *fard* (obligatory) re-performance and mere validity in cases of minor, unnoticed impurities.
